params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to event-level reshaped views (events_params_kv, events_items_flat, events_user_properties_kv) using the event-level keys (event_date, event_timestamp, event_bundle_sequence_id, user_pseudo_id) — these reshaped views are 1:1 with events_base at the event grain, so measures computed on events_base are not duplicated when joined. | Safe join example: JOIN events_params_kv USING (event_date, event_timestamp, event_bundle_sequence_id, user_pseudo_id) — safe because events_params_kv is a reshape of event_params and preserves one row per event. | Safe join example: JOIN events_items_flat USING (event_date, event_timestamp, event_bundle_sequence_id, user_pseudo_id) only when that view is known to be one-row-per-item-per-event; if it is one-row-per-event-item then joining will expand rows and multiply event-level measures — aggregate items first (e.g., SUM(item_revenue) PARTITION BY event keys) before joining back to avoid duplication. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example, an items table that contains multiple rows per event or a params_kv that is multi-row per event) without re-aggregation. Such joins will multiply event-level counts and sums. If you need item-level detail and want event-level measures preserved, first aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per event (e.g., GROUP BY event_date, event_timestamp, event_bundle_sequence_id, user_pseudo_id) and then join. | When joining to user-level or session-level aggregates (user_last_event_rank, user_cumulative_revenue, user_event_sequences): join on user_pseudo_id (and optionally user_first_touch_timestamp or other session keys) — ensure those views are aggregated to one row per user (or per user/session key) to avoid duplicating event rows. For example, JOIN user_cumulative_revenue USING (user_pseudo_id) is safe only if user_cumulative_revenue is one-row-per-user; if it is one-row-per-user-date, join on both user_pseudo_id and date. | When composing higher-level metrics, prefer: 1) aggregate events_base to desired grain (e.g., by user or session) using GROUP BY, 2) join pre-aggregated dimension tables or metrics that are at the same grain. Never rely on implicit de-duplication by joins; explicitly aggregate the many-side first.

views.name: events_params_kv
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  event_date,
  event_timestamp,
  event_bundle_sequence_id,
  user_pseudo_id,
  event_name,
  param.key AS param_key,
  COALESCE(param.value.string_value, CAST(param.value.int_value AS STRING), CAST(param.value.double_value AS STRING), CAST(param.value.float_value AS STRING)) AS param_value_string,
  param.value.int_value AS param_value_int,
  param.value.float_value AS param_value_float
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`,
UNNEST(event_params) AS param
grain: one row per event_param (event * param key)

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

params.description: Provides one row per event parameter (event × parameter key) for GA4 events, exposing param key and typed values alongside event identifiers and timestamps.
params.when_to_use: Look up or filter events by a specific parameter key or value (e.g., find events where param 'item_id' = '123'). | Build metrics or aggregations that depend on parameter values after grouping by event-level identifiers (e.g., count distinct events that contain a parameter key). | Join parameter-level data back to event-level records (after appropriate aggregation) to enrich event dimensions with parameter-derived attributes. | Pivot or reshape parameters into columns (param key → column) by aggregating param_value_string/int/float per event and key.
params.output_schema: table_suffix: the _TABLE_SUFFIX value from the source table name pattern (bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*); indicates the source partition/table shard | event_date: event_date from the source events table (string/date in source) — the event's calendar date | event_timestamp: event_timestamp from the source events table (integer/micros) — raw event timestamp | event_bundle_sequence_id: event_bundle_sequence_id from the source events table — the bundle/sequence id that groups events | user_pseudo_id: user_pseudo_id from the source events table — anonymized user identifier for the event | event_name: event_name from the source events table — the name/type of the event | param_key: param.key from UNNEST(event_params) — the parameter key for this row | param_value_string: COALESCE(param.value.string_value, CAST(param.value.int_value AS STRING), CAST(param.value.double_value AS STRING), CAST(param.value.float_value AS STRING)) — a string representation of the parameter value if present | param_value_int: param.value.int_value — the integer typed parameter value (nullable) | param_value_float: param.value.float_value — the floating/double typed parameter value (nullable)
params.grounded_columns: bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*.event_date | bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*.event_timestamp | bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*.event_bundle_sequence_id | bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*.user_pseudo_id | bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*.event_name | bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*.event_params (UNNEST -> param.key, param.value.*) | _TABLE_SUFFIX (metadata from the wildcard table reference)
params.metric: This view is a reshape (no aggregated metrics). Derived columns are direct projections or casts from base fields. Example derived expressions: | param_value_string = COALESCE(param.value.string_value, CAST(param.value.int_value AS STRING), CAST(param.value.double_value AS STRING), CAST(param.value.float_value AS STRING)) | param_value_int = param.value.int_value | param_value_float = param.value.float_value
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to event-level or one-row-per-event views on the composite event key (event_date, event_timestamp, event_bundle_sequence_id, user_pseudo_id, event_name) — safe because this view is one row per (event × param_key), and joining to one-row-per-event will not duplicate event-level columns if you intend to keep parameter rows. If your target is to retain event_rows multiplicity, join keys example: events_base on (event_date, event_timestamp, event_bundle_sequence_id, user_pseudo_id, event_name). | To avoid measure duplication when you need event-level aggregates, first aggregate this view up to event granularity (e.g., any aggregation that yields one row per event such as MAX(CASE WHEN param_key='X' THEN param_value_string END) per event) and then join to other event-level tables/views. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables relative to events (for example: events_items_flat or other item-level/join views that are one row per item per event) unless you intend row multiplication. Joining events_params_kv to events_items_flat on event keys will produce a cartesian-like multiplication for events that have multiple params and multiple items — re-aggregate one side first to preserve correct measures. | Safe to join to user-level aggregates (one row per user) on user_pseudo_id when you want per-user enrichment, because events_params_kv rows will attach to the user row (this multiplies parameter rows per user as expected). If you need to compute user-level metrics from these rows, perform aggregation after the join or aggregate events_params_kv to user-level first. | When composing higher-level metrics (counts, distinct counts) using this view, aggregate on event identifiers to avoid counting the same event multiple times due to multiple parameters. Example safe pattern: COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(CAST(event_timestamp AS STRING), user_pseudo_id, CAST(event_bundle_sequence_id AS STRING))) as distinct_event_count after selecting the desired filter on param_key/value. | If joining to sibling reshape views (events_user_properties_kv, events_items_flat), be explicit about desired granularity: either (a) join after aggregating both sides to a common grain, or (b) accept multiplicative semantics when the analysis intends to count parameter×item combinations.

views.description: Unnested event parameters as one row per event_param key/value. Preserves event identifiers to join back to events. | Use for: Filter events by specific event_param key/value; Pivot event_params into event-level columns; Count occurrences of param values over time

params.description: A flattened, one-row-per-item-within-an-event view of GA4 event records — answers item-level questions within event context (e.g., item revenue, price, quantity per event).
params.when_to_use: Get item-level details for each event (e.g., list every item purchased/viewed in each event). | Compute event-item level aggregations after safe aggregation (e.g., sum item_revenue by event_date or user). | Join item-level event rows to dimensions keyed at the event or user level (when join keys preserve one-row-per-item cardinality). | Serve as the base for building higher-level metrics (daily top items, per-user item totals) after correct grouping/aggregation.
params.output_schema: table_suffix: BigQuery table shard suffix from source (_TABLE_SUFFIX). Source: _TABLE_SUFFIX from FROM `...events_*`. | event_date: Date of the event as stored in the source events table. Source: event_date. | event_timestamp: Event timestamp (nanoseconds/microseconds as in source). Source: event_timestamp. | event_bundle_sequence_id: Sequence id for the event bundle grouping in GA4. Source: event_bundle_sequence_id. | user_pseudo_id: Pseudo user identifier assigned by GA4. Source: user_pseudo_id. | event_name: Name of the GA4 event (e.g., purchase, view_item). Source: event_name. | item_id: Item identifier from the event's items repeated field. Source: items.item_id. | item_name: Item name from the event's items repeated field. Source: items.item_name. | item_brand: Item brand from the event's items repeated field. Source: items.item_brand. | item_category: Item category from the event's items repeated field. Source: items.item_category. | item_price: Item price in the event's currency (as reported). Source: items.price. | item_price_in_usd: Item price converted to USD (if provided). Source: items.price_in_usd. | item_quantity: Quantity of the item in this event. Source: items.quantity. | item_revenue: Revenue attributed to this item in event currency (items.item_revenue). Source: items.item_revenue. | item_revenue_in_usd: Revenue attributed to this item in USD (items.item_revenue_in_usd). Source: items.item_revenue_in_usd. | item_affiliation: Affiliation field for the item (e.g., store/channel). Source: items.affiliation.
params.grounded_columns: _TABLE_SUFFIX | event_date | event_timestamp | event_bundle_sequence_id | user_pseudo_id | event_name | items.item_id | items.item_name | items.item_brand | items.item_category | items.price | items.price_in_usd | items.quantity | items.item_revenue | items.item_revenue_in_usd | items.affiliation
params.metric: item_revenue = items.item_revenue (raw item-level revenue value as provided per item in the event) | item_revenue_in_usd = items.item_revenue_in_usd (raw item-level revenue in USD as provided) | item_price = items.price (raw item price per unit in event currency) | item_price_in_usd = items.price_in_usd (raw item price per unit in USD) | item_quantity = items.quantity (raw quantity for the item in this event)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to events_base (or any event-level view keyed by event_date, event_timestamp, event_bundle_sequence_id, user_pseudo_id, event_name) ON those exact event keys — safe because this view is already one-row-per-item-per-event; joining to event-level one-row-per-event tables will not duplicate item rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user-level dimensions keyed by user_pseudo_id (e.g., user profile table with one row per user_pseudo_id) ON user_pseudo_id — safe because user-level tables are one-row-per-user, so each item row remains distinct and measures (item_revenue, item_quantity) are not multiplied. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join directly to any other repeated/one-to-many view (for example, events_params_kv, events_user_properties_kv, or any params/kv reshape view) on event-level keys without first aggregating those one-to-many sides to one row per event or per item. Those joins would multiply rows and duplicate item-level measures. Instead, either: |   - aggregate the one-to-many side to the same grain (one row per event or one row per event*item) before joining, or |   - join via a DISTINCT/UNNEST-aware approach that preserves cardinality, or |   - re-aggregate after the join (e.g., SUM(item_revenue) GROUP BY desired keys) to remove duplication. | unsafe join examples: do NOT join directly to events_params_kv on event keys if events_params_kv has multiple param rows per event — this will multiply item rows and overcount item_revenue unless you pre-aggregate params to one row per event. | note on joins that change measures: if you join to a many-to-one dimension from the item row (e.g., lookup by item_id to an items master table keyed uniquely by item_id), that is safe because the dimension is one-row-per-item_id and will not duplicate measures. Explicit guidance: join to item master tables ON item_id when the master is unique on item_id — safe. | final planner tip: treat this view's intrinsic measures (item_revenue, item_revenue_in_usd, item_quantity) as item-level atomic measures. Any joins that increase the number of rows per original (event,item) must be followed by correct aggregation (SUM/AVG/COUNT DISTINCT as appropriate) to avoid double counting.

Exposes item identifiers, price/quantity/revenue fields and preserves event-level identifiers and context for aggregations at item or event granularity. | Use for: Top items by revenue or quantity; Item-level revenue/time trends; Join items to product dimension if available

views.name: daily_event_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  event_date,
  event_name,
  COUNT(1) AS events_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) AS unique_users,
  SUM(event_value_in_usd) AS sum_event_value_in_usd,
  SUM(ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd) AS sum_ecommerce_purchase_revenue_in_usd,
  SUM(ecommerce.total_item_quantity) AS sum_ecommerce_total_item_quantity
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
GROUP BY _TABLE_SUFFIX, event_date, event_name

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use BETWEEN or IN to restrict date range in outer query

params.description: Daily, per-source-table and per-event aggregation of event counts, distinct users, and several event/ecommerce numeric sums.
params.when_to_use: Get daily event-level KPIs (counts, unique users, USD sums) for a specific event_name or set of event_names. | Compare event volume or revenue across dates or across source tables (sharded by _TABLE_SUFFIX). | Serve as a aggregation basis to build higher-level metrics (e.g., weekly/monthly totals) by further time-window aggregation. | Join to one-row-per-table or one-row-per-user dimension tables (with care) to add attributes without changing measures.
params.output_schema: table_suffix: the source table shard name (_TABLE_SUFFIX) from which rows were read (derived from _TABLE_SUFFIX). | event_date: calendar date of the event (derived from event_date). | event_name: name/type of the event (derived from event_name). | events_count: number of event rows in that (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) group; derived from COUNT(1). | unique_users: number of distinct user_pseudo_id values in that group; derived from COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id). | sum_event_value_in_usd: sum of event_value_in_usd for rows in that group; derived from SUM(event_value_in_usd). | sum_ecommerce_purchase_revenue_in_usd: sum of ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd for rows in that group; derived from SUM(ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd). | sum_ecommerce_total_item_quantity: sum of ecommerce.total_item_quantity for rows in that group; derived from SUM(ecommerce.total_item_quantity).
params.grounded_columns: _TABLE_SUFFIX | event_date | event_name | user_pseudo_id | event_value_in_usd | ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd | ecommerce.total_item_quantity
params.metric: events_count = COUNT(1) over group (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) as integer event volume | unique_users = COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) over group (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) as distinct user count | sum_event_value_in_usd = SUM(event_value_in_usd) over group (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) as numeric sum of event_value_in_usd | sum_ecommerce_purchase_revenue_in_usd = SUM(ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd) over group (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) as numeric sum of ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd | sum_ecommerce_total_item_quantity = SUM(ecommerce.total_item_quantity) over group (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) as numeric sum of ecommerce.total_item_quantity
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension view that is one-row-per-table_suffix (or has table_suffix as a key) on table_suffix — safe because this view is one-row-per (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) and joining on table_suffix alone will not multiplicatively duplicate measures if the dimension is one-row-per-table_suffix. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-user view keyed by user_pseudo_id (e.g., a user profile table) on user_pseudo_id only after first rolling this view up to the user level (or by joining on user_pseudo_id via a subquery that re-aggregates user measures), because this view only contains aggregated distinct user counts (unique_users) and does not retain individual user rows. | do NOT directly join this view to a one-to-many detail table (for example, events_items_flat or events_params_kv) on keys that allow multiple detail rows per (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) without re-aggregating — such joins will multiply events_count and the SUM metrics. If you must enrich with many-rows-per-event data, first aggregate the detail table to the same grain (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) producing measures, then join on (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) and combine measures (e.g., sum or avg) as appropriate. | do NOT join to sibling reshape views (events_params_kv, events_items_flat, events_user_properties_kv) directly unless those siblings are pre-aggregated to (table_suffix, event_date, event_name). Those sibling views are typically one-to-many per event and will duplicate aggregation if joined directly. | safe composition pattern to add dimensions: (1) optionally filter or aggregate this view to a coarser grain (e.g., by event_date only) using SUM/COUNT/DISTINCT over the output columns, (2) join to one-row-per-key dimension tables on matching keys, ensuring the dimension does not introduce multiplicity, or (3) if joining to many-rows-per-key dimensions, perform the join inside a subquery that re-aggregates back to the intended grain. | example safe join keys: (table_suffix), (event_date) after appropriate re-aggregation, or (table_suffix, event_date, event_name) to join to any other pre-aggregated view at the exact same grain — safe because identical-grain joins preserve 1:1 mapping between aggregated rows and will not duplicate measures.

views.description: Daily aggregated counts and basic revenue sums by event_date and event_name. Useful for time series of event volumes and revenues. Aggregates at the shard/event_date grain; callers should restrict _TABLE_SUFFIX to control the date window. | Use for: Daily event volume and revenue trends; Comparing event types by day; Feeding dashboards with daily aggregates

views.name: user_last_event_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  event_date,
  user_pseudo_id,
  event_timestamp,
  event_bundle_sequence_id,
  event_name,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_pseudo_id ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC, event_bundle_sequence_id DESC) AS rn,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_pseudo_id ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC) AS rnk
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
grain: one row per event with rank columns per user_pseudo_id

views.name: user_event_sequences

SELECT
  base._TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  base.event_date AS event_date,
  base.user_pseudo_id AS user_pseudo_id,

  base.event_name AS event_name,
